label: broken

unstated.what: On the oracle dialect, an explicit table alias (FROM tbl AS a) must produce no AL01 violation even when the user explicitly configures rules.aliasing.table.aliasing = implicit, which normally flags and removes an explicit AS. The stated bug only covers the default config flagging a missing AS.

instruction_covers: Oracle implicit table alias (FROM customers base / FROM tbl a) must not raise AL01
The failure is the AL01 rule (aliasing.table) demanding an AS keyword Oracle table aliases do not support
Expected result is no lint violations for the oracle repro
notes: Repo verified: AL01._eval flags a missing AS whenever aliasing != 'implicit' and removes an explicit AS when aliasing == 'implicit' (src/sqlfluff/rules/aliasing/AL01.py:73-115); default aliasing is explicit (core/default_config.cfg). Oracle inherits the ansi AliasExpressionSegment where AS is optional, so 'FROM tbl AS a' already parses (no PRS) and is not flagged under the default explicit config — those assertions (test 3, the no-PRS assertions, AL02 column-alias cases, ansi/bigquery still flagged) are pre-existing and preserved by any oracle-only fix (R3). The implicit-config variant is a config value the instruction never names; grep surfaces it (config_info.py validation ['implicit','explicit']), but the minimal fix of the stated bug — stop flagging a missing AS on oracle — leaves the remove-AS branch intact and still fails test 4, so the exemption-overriding-explicit-user-config is new semantics (R2 not_inferable). Environment/dbt framing is out of scope.
